This document contains the code used for harmonizing and visualizing the raw MMS concentration-response data extracted from literature as described in 'Advancing AOPs for genotoxicity through quantifying KERs linking DNA alkylation to increase in mutations and chromosome aberrations' by Winkelman et al., 2026.

```{r,warning=F, message=F}
library(readxl)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(clinPK)
library(ggplot2)
library(mice)
library(lme4)
library(splines)
library(lmerTest)
library(partR2)
library(stats)
source('Functions_data_wrangling.R')
```

Comet assay
-----------

##General data wrangling##


General first steps in data wrangling
```{r}
#Read in the data
comet = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202604141723_Data_from_literature_search_MMS_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'Comet assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
comet = generalwrangle(comet, conc_col = "Concentration MMS")

#Convert data classess
comet = correctclass(comet)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(comet)
```

Looks good

Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
which(comet$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0)
```
Subtraction from background did not occur.

Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(comet$`Concentration MMS` == 0)
length(unique(comet$`Study index`))
```
We seem to have a study with a missing 0 concentration, let's examine which one this is
```{r}
comet %>%
  group_by(`Study index`) %>%
  filter(!(any(`Concentration MMS` == 0, na.rm = TRUE)))
```
Unfortunately we will have to take this study out

```{r}
comet = comet[comet$DOI != '10.1038/s41598-018-20995-w',]
```

Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(comet$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```
We have no missing replicates

Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
comet = remove_few_obs_studies(comet)
```


##Check outcome units##

```{r}
table(comet$`Outcome unit (eg % of DNA in tail)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

Standardize nomenclature for outcome units
```{r}
comet$`Outcome unit (eg % of DNA in tail)`[comet$`Outcome unit (eg % of DNA in tail)` != "migration (µm)"] = '% DNA in tail'
```



##Conversions

Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(comet$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```
The full range of data over replicates is hard to convert unless there are only 2 replicates, in that case the full range equals mean +/- SD, let's check if that is the case

```{r}
comet %>%
  filter(comet$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)` == 'Full range over replicates') %>%
  select(c(`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, replicates))
```

This is indeed the case

```{r}
comet$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`[comet$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)` == 'Full range over replicates'] = 'SD'
```

Convert variability estimates to SDs and SEMs
```{r}
comet = convert_varest(comet)
```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
comet = convert_to_FC(comet, conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
table(comet$`Concentration unit (eg μg/ml or μM)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

```{r}
MMS_g_per_mol = 110.13 #Derived from pubchem https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4156
comet = convert_concs(comet, MMS_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
comet = convert_CTassaytype(comet)
```

Standardize scoring techniques
```{r}
comet = convert_scoringTechnique(comet)
```



##Check for cytotoxicity

We have one study where significant hedgehogs were reported, we'll mark this observation as cytotoxic
```{r}
comet$ct[comet$Comments == "Singificant hedgehogs" & !(is.na(comet$Comments))] = F
```


See where there is cytotoxicity data missing (if at all)
```{r}
unique(comet[,c(2:4)][is.na(comet$`Relative survival (%)`),])
```

We have five missing studies with missing information on cytotoxicity

The Kuehner study only has missing cytotox data on one concentration and higher concentrations are reported non-cytotoxic, we will therefore assume that the full range is non-cytotoxic
```{r}
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1007/s00204-013-1060-2'] = T
```


The closest study in design (for which we have cytotox data) to the study of Collia, the study of Li, the study of Kawaguchi and the study of Speit 2016, is the Speit 2014 study after 2h of exposure, in the Speit study, we see significant hedgehogs occur at 800 uM, all concentrations below show no excessive cytotox
```{r}
#Collia 2024
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.tox.2023.153690' & comet$`Concentration MMS` >= 800] = F
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.tox.2023.153690' & comet$`Concentration MMS` < 800] = T

#Li 2022
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/nargab/lqac065' & comet$`Concentration MMS` >= 800] = F
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/nargab/lqac065' & comet$`Concentration MMS` < 800] = T

#Kawaguchi 2010
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.4061/2010/541050' & comet$`Concentration MMS` >= 800] = F
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.4061/2010/541050' & comet$`Concentration MMS` < 800] = T

#Speit 2016
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2016.05.001' & comet$`Concentration MMS` >= 800] = F
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2016.05.001' & comet$`Concentration MMS` < 800] = T
```

For the Azqueta study, no cytotoxicity assay was performed, but it was suggested that the deviating tail intensity at the highest concentration could be explained through cytotox, we will mark this observation as cytotoxic and will assume the other concentrations are not
```{r}
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geq105' & comet$`Concentration MMS` >= 600] = F
comet$ct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geq105' & comet$`Concentration MMS` < 600] = T
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(comet$ct) / nrow(comet)
comet = comet[comet$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
comet = remove_few_obs_studies(comet)
```


##Plot data##

Before plotting, there are a few more things to do:
The Collia and Azqueta 2011 studies reported multiple dose-responses where the only difference was the types of slides that were used for scoring or scoring technique itself, since the results of the different methods are not entirely independent, we will only use the data pertaining to the most commonly used techniques.

Only keep the Azqueta and Collia data for the image analysis on glass slides scored using comet IV
```{r}
#Azqueta paper
comet = comet[!(comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geq105' & !(comet$Comments == 'Image analysis of gels on glass slides' & comet$`Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` == 'Semi-automated (Comet IV)')),]

#Collia paper
comet = comet[!(comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.tox.2023.153690' & !(comet$Comments == 'DNA damage measured using classic 2gel/slide')),]
```


The Li study reported 4 dose-responses which are quarters of a 386 well plate and can be considered technical replicates, here we summarize over the technical replicates to get joint means and SDs
```{r}
cometLi = comet[comet$DOI == '10.1093/nargab/lqac065',]
cometLi$`Study index` = as.numeric(cometLi$`Study index`)

#Take the first quarter well plate (arbitrary) for later merging
cometLi1 = cometLi[cometLi$`Study index` == min(cometLi$`Study index`),]

summary_data = cometLi %>%
  group_by(`Concentration MMS`) %>%  
  summarise(
    grand_mean = sum(replicates * `Outcome for the treatment`) / sum(replicates),
    grand_variance = {
      # Calculate within-group sum of squares
      within_var = sum((replicates - 1) * (SD^2))
      # Calculate between-group sum of squares
      between_var = sum(replicates * (`Outcome for the treatment` - 
                       (sum(replicates * `Outcome for the treatment`) / sum(replicates)))^2)
      # Total variance
      (within_var + between_var) / (sum(replicates) - 1)
    },
    grand_SD = sqrt(grand_variance)
  )


cometLi = cometLi1 %>%
  left_join(summary_data, by = "Concentration MMS") %>%
  mutate(
    `Outcome for the treatment` = grand_mean,
    `Outcome variability lower estimate` = grand_mean - grand_SD,
    `Outcome variability upper estimate` = grand_mean + grand_SD
  ) %>%
  select(-grand_mean, -grand_variance, -grand_SD)  

#Replace the dose-responses per technical replicate by summary dose-response
comet = comet[comet$DOI != '10.1093/nargab/lqac065',]
comet = rbind(comet, cometLi)
```


Add a column to map scoring techniques to automated, semi-automated or manual
```{r}
comet = comet %>%
  mutate(
    `Scoring automation` = case_when(
      `Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` %in% 
        c("manual") ~ "Manual",
      `Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` %in% 
        c("CA4", "Semi-automated (Comet IV)") ~ "Semi-automated",
      `Technique for scoring (eg manual / automated)` %in% 
        c("Automated (IMSTAR)", "clrmorph", "CeligoS", "Komet6" ) ~ "Automated"
    )
  )
```


Split the data into the unmodified comet assay and the enzyme modified comet assays
```{r}
comet = comet %>%
  mutate(enzyme_modification = case_when(
    Comments == "Fpg modified comet assay" ~ 'Fpg modified',
    Comments == 'hAAG modified comet assay, Cytotoxicity valuesderived from Azqueta 2013, RSG = relative suspension growth' ~ 'hAAG modified',
    Comments == 'hAAG modified comet assay, Both commercial and non-commercial FPG data was reported in this paper, we extracted only the non-commercial data since that matches with the results from the Murazabal 2020 study' ~ 'hAAG modified',
    Comments == "Fpg modified comet assay, Both commercial and non-commercial FPG data was reported in this paper, we extracted only the non-commercial data since that matches with the results from the Murazabal 2020 study" ~ 'Fpg modified',
    Comments == 'Fpg modified comet assay, Cytotoxicity valuesderived from Azqueta 2013, RSG = relative suspension growth' ~ 'Fpg modified',
    T ~'Unmodified'
  ))

comet$enzyme_modification = as.factor(comet$enzyme_modification)
```

```{r}
cometall = comet
cometenz = comet[comet$enzyme_modification != 'Unmodified',]
cometFpg = cometenz[cometenz$enzyme_modification == 'Fpg modified',]
comethAAG = cometenz[cometenz$enzyme_modification == 'hAAG modified',]
comet = comet[comet$enzyme_modification == 'Unmodified',]
```



Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper

Create a separate column to identify enzyme modified comet assays


```{r}
comet$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(comet))

#Shi 2010 paper
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2010.01.008' & comet$`Time of exposure [h]` == 4] = '4h exposure'
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2010.01.008' & comet$`Time of exposure [h]` == 24] = '24h exposure'

#Azqueta 2011 paper
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geq105'] = '2011, Unmodified'

#Azqueta 2013 paper
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/get002' & comet$Comments == 'Fpg modified comet assay'] = '2013, Fpg modified'
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/get002' & is.na(comet$Comments)] = '2013, Unmodified'

#Speit 2014 paper
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geu015' & comet$`Time of exposure [h]` == 2] = '2014, 2h exposure'
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geu015' & comet$`Time of exposure [h]` == 4] = '2014, 4h exposure'

#Speit 2016 paper
comet$distinct[comet$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2016.05.001'] = '2016'
```


```{r}
doseres_plot(comet, 'all data', assay = 'Comet_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
doseres_contrast(comet, 'Exposure times and scoring automation', assay = 'Comet_Assay', color_col = 'Time of exposure [h]', shape_col = 'Scoring automation', linetype_col = 'Outcome unit (eg % of DNA in tail)', solid_level = '% DNA in tail', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
```

The Li study seems insensitive, likely due the fact that its exposure time is much lower compared to any other tested exposure time

```{r}
doseres_contrast(cometenz, 'Enzyme modification MMS', assay = 'Comet_Assay', color_col = 'enzyme_modification', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS', save = T, path = '../Figures/ConcRes_comparison/FigS1')
```

#Variance decomposition


```{r}
cometmod = comet
names(cometmod) = make.names(names(cometmod))
```

```{r}
cometimp = mice(cometmod, m = 1, method = 'pmm', seed = 20260205)
```


```{r}
cometimp2 = complete(cometimp, 1)[,c('Author', 'DOI', 'Study.index', 'FC', 'Concentration.MMS', 'Time.of.exposure..h.', 'Outcome.unit..eg...of.DNA.in.tail.', 'Scoring.automation', 'Relative.survival....')]

```

```{r}
any(is.na(cometimp2))
cometimp2 = prepare_varcomp(cometimp2, cometmod)
```

```{r,message=F}
model_comet = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2) +
       Time.of.exposure..h. +
       Outcome.unit..eg...of.DNA.in.tail. +
       Scoring.automation +
       Relative.survival.... +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = cometimp2
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_comet))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

cometVAR = partR2(model_comet, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2)",
                               "Time.of.exposure..h.",
                               "Outcome.unit..eg...of.DNA.in.tail.",
                               "Scoring.automation",
                               "Relative.survival...."))
cometVAR$R2
cometVAR$model = model_comet
cometVAR$vc = vc
```

##Check for cytotoxicity

```{r}
unique(MN[,c(2:4)][is.na(MN$`Relative survival (%)`),])
```

We have quite some studies with missing cytotoxicity measurements, here's a summary of what we found after looking into this:
- The Bryce 2010 paper, the Bemis 2015, as well as the Kawaguchi 2010 paper did not provide viability estimates per concentration but stated that the relative survival at the highest tested concentrations was above 50%, therefore all of its datapoints are kept.
- For the Chapman 2015 paper, not every concentration was tested for cytotox, but given that no cytotox was reported at higher concentrations than the ones omitted, all observations will be kept
- The Yamamoto 2013 paper did not report cytotox but similar concentrations were not reported cytotoxic in similar studies like Verma 2016 and Bryce 2007 so the observations will be kept
- The Chapman 2014 paper did not report cytotox but similar concentrations were not reported cytotoxic in similar studies like Chapman 2015 so the observations will be kept

```{r}
MN$ct[is.na(MN$ct)] = T
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(MN$ct) / nrow(MN)
MN = MN[MN$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
MN = remove_few_obs_studies(MN)
```



#Plotting the data

Optimize variables for plotting and Variance decomposition
```{r}
#Add a column for S9 status
MN$S9 = !(is.na(MN$`S9 source (eg. Rat liver)`))
MN$S9 = factor(MN$S9, labels = c("no", "yes"))

#Add a column for expression period in days
MN$expression_period = (MN$`Time of harvest [h]` - MN$`Time of exposure [h]`) / 24

#Ensure Cytochalasin B variable has two levels only
MN$`Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)` = factor(tolower(MN$`Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)`))

#Add a column to map scoring techniques to microscopy based, flow cytometry based or hybrid
MN = MN %>%
  mutate(
    `Scoring technique` = case_when(
      `Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)` %in% 
        c("manual", "semiManualMicroscope", "Metafer", "cellAnalyzer6K") ~ "Microscopy",
      `Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)` %in% 
        c("flowCyto", "Coulter") ~ "Flow Cytometry",
      `Technique for scoring micronuclei (eg manual or automated)` %in% 
        c("imageStream") ~ "Hybrid"
    ), `Assay type` = case_when(
      `Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)` == 'yes' ~ 'CBMN',
      `Cytochalasin B present (yes / no)` == 'no' ~ 'conventional'
    )
  )
```


Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(MN$Author))
length(unique(MN$`Study index`))
```

Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper
```{r}
MN$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(MN))

#Zhang 1995 paper
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/0165-7992(95)00027-5' & MN$`Time of harvest [h]` == 28] = '28h harvest'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/0165-7992(95)00027-5' & MN$`Time of harvest [h]` == 52] = '52h harvest'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/0165-7992(95)00027-5' & MN$`Time of harvest [h]` == 76] = '76h harvest'

#Sanders 2022 paper
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geac025' & MN$`Time of exposure [h]` == 3] = '3h exposure'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geac025' & MN$`Time of exposure [h]` == 24] = '24h exposure'

#Avlasevich 2021
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geab039' & is.na(MN$`S9 (%)`)] = '+S9'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geab039' & !(is.na(MN$`S9 (%)`))] = '-S9'

#Bryce 2010
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2010.08.020.' & MN$`Study index` == 11] = 'repeat 1'
MN$distinct[MN$DOI == '10.1016/j.mrgentox.2010.08.020.' & MN$`Study index` == 12] = 'repeat 2'

```


##Variance decomposition

```{r}
MNmod = MN
names(MNmod) = make.names(names(MNmod))
```

Run imputation
```{r}
MNimp = mice(MNmod, m = 1, method = 'pmm', seed = 20260205)
MNimp = complete(MNimp, 1)

MNimp2 = prepare_varcomp(MNimp, MNmod)
MNimp2 = MNimp2[,c('Author', 'Study.index', 'DOI', 'FC', 'FClog', 'Concentration.MMS', 'Time.of.exposure..h.', 'expression_period', 'S9', 'Assay.type', 'Scoring.technique', 'Relative.survival....', 'FC_SEMlog')]

any(is.na(MNimp2))
```

```{r,message=F}
model_MN = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2) +
       Time.of.exposure..h. +
       expression_period +
       S9 + 
       Assay.type + 
       Scoring.technique +
       Relative.survival.... +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = MNimp2
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_MN))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

MNVAR = partR2(model_MN, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2)",
                               "Time.of.exposure..h.",
                               "expression_period",
                               "S9",
                               "Assay.type",
                               "Scoring.technique",
                               "Relative.survival...."
                               ), R2_type = 'marginal'
       )

MNVAR$R2
MNVAR$model = model_MN
MNVAR$vc = vc
```




-----------
gh2ax assay
-----------


##General data wrangling##


General first steps in data wrangling
```{r}
#Read in the data
gh2ax = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202604141723_Data_from_literature_search_MMS_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'gH2AX assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
gh2ax = generalwrangle(gh2ax, conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')

#Convert data classess
gh2ax = correctclass(gh2ax)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(gh2ax)
```
Looks good


Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
gh2ax[which(gh2ax$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0),]
```

We see no subtraction from background 


Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(gh2ax$`Concentration MMS` == 0)
length(unique(gh2ax$`Study index`))
```
We have more controls than study indexes, let's see if this is the case because we have raw datapoints

```{r}
any(gh2ax$replicates == 1)
```

Indeed, let's try to summarize the individual measurements

```{r}
gh2ax = ObsToMeans(gh2ax, varOI = 'Study index', ct = T, varextra = NA)
```

Let's check if we still have more controls than datapoints

```{r}
sum(gh2ax$`Concentration MMS` == 0)
length(unique(gh2ax$`Study index`))
```
We seem to have two studies with missing controls, let's examine which ones those are

```{r}
gh2ax %>%
  group_by(`Study index`) %>%
  filter(.data$`Concentration MMS` == min(.data$`Concentration MMS`, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(1:4, `Concentration MMS`, `Outcome unit (eg mean fluorescence intensity)`)
```

The two studies where we have a missing 0 concentration both report fold changes so the studies can be kept

Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(gh2ax$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```
We have no missing replicates

Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
gh2ax = remove_few_obs_studies(gh2ax)
```


##Check outcome units

```{r}
table(gh2ax$`Outcome unit (eg mean fluorescence intensity)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

let's recode so that the same outcomes are grouped together:

```{r}
gh2ax <- gh2ax %>%
  mutate(`Outcome unit (eg mean fluorescence intensity)` =
    case_when(
      `Outcome unit (eg mean fluorescence intensity)` %in% c(
        "Multiflow",
        "mean fluorescenec intesity/cell",
        "Fold change in median fluorescence intensity"
      ) ~ "MFI",
      
      TRUE ~ `Outcome unit (eg mean fluorescence intensity)`
    )
  )
```


##Conversions


Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(gh2ax$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

Calculate SEMs
```{r}
gh2ax = convert_varest(gh2ax)
```

We will exclude the FC data with a missing control for now and then add it back to the data later
```{r}
gh2axMissingCtrl = gh2ax %>%
  group_by(`Study index`) %>%
  filter(!any(`Concentration MMS` == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

gh2axOther = gh2ax %>%
  group_by(`Study index`) %>%
  filter(any(`Concentration MMS` == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
gh2axOther = convert_to_FC(gh2axOther, conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')

gh2axMissingCtrl$control_response = NA
gh2axMissingCtrl$control_SD = NA
gh2axMissingCtrl$FC = gh2axMissingCtrl$`Outcome for the treatment`
gh2axMissingCtrl$FC_SD = gh2axMissingCtrl$SD
gh2axMissingCtrl$FC_SEM = gh2axMissingCtrl$SEM
gh2axMissingCtrl$FC_lower = gh2axMissingCtrl$`Outcome variability lower estimate`
gh2axMissingCtrl$FC_upper = gh2axMissingCtrl$`Outcome variability upper estimate`

gh2ax = rbind(gh2axOther, gh2axMissingCtrl)
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
gh2ax = convert_concs(gh2ax, MMS_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
gh2ax = convert_CTassaytype(gh2ax)
```

Standardize scoring techniques
```{r}
gh2ax = convert_scoringTechnique(gh2ax)
```


##Check for cytotoxicity

```{r}
unique(gh2ax[,c(2:4)][is.na(gh2ax$`Relative survival (%)`),])
```
We have two studies with missing cytotox data.
The Avlasevich 2023 study and Avlasevich 2021 study indicate that for both 4 and 24 hours of exposure, severe cytotox is observed starting from ~100uM
We will use this threshold to indicate cytotox for the the Riches and Bryce studies


```{r}
gh2ax$ct[is.na(gh2ax$`Relative survival (%)`) & gh2ax$`Concentration MMS` > 100] = F
gh2ax$ct[is.na(gh2ax$`Relative survival (%)`) & gh2ax$`Concentration MMS` <= 100] = T
```


Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(gh2ax$ct) / nrow(gh2ax)
gh2ax = gh2ax[gh2ax$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
gh2ax = remove_few_obs_studies(gh2ax)
```


#Plotting the data

```{r}
gh2ax$S9 = !(is.na(gh2ax$`S9 source (eg. Rat liver)`))
gh2ax$S9 = factor(gh2ax$S9, labels = c("no", "yes"))
```

Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(gh2ax$Author))
length(unique(gh2ax$`Study index`))
```

Define distinctive features of studies from the same paper
```{r}
gh2ax$distinct = rep(NA, nrow(gh2ax))

#Avlasevich 2021 paper
gh2ax$distinct[gh2ax$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geab039' & gh2ax$`Time of exposure [h]` == 24 & !(is.na(gh2ax$`S9 (%)`))] = '2021, 24h exposure +S9'
gh2ax$distinct[gh2ax$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geab039' & gh2ax$`Time of exposure [h]` == 24 & is.na(gh2ax$`S9 (%)`)] = '2021, 24h exposure'
gh2ax$distinct[gh2ax$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geab039' & gh2ax$`Time of exposure [h]` == 4 & is.na(gh2ax$`S9 (%)`)] = '2021, 4h exposure +S9'
gh2ax$distinct[gh2ax$DOI == '10.1093/mutage/geab039' & gh2ax$`Time of exposure [h]` == 4 & !(is.na(gh2ax$`S9 (%)`))] = '2021, 4h exposure'


#Avlasevich 2023 paper
gh2ax$distinct[gh2ax$DOI == 'unpublished' & gh2ax$`Time of exposure [h]` == 4] = '2023, 4h exposure -S9'

```

```{r}
#Simplify and standardize naming for scoring techniques
gh2ax = gh2ax %>%
  mutate(
    `Scoring technique` = case_when(
      `Type of measurement (eg Microscopic imaging or flow cytometry)` %in% 
        c("manual", "Cell Analyzer 6000", "cellAnalyzer6K") ~ "Microscopy",
      `Type of measurement (eg Microscopic imaging or flow cytometry)` %in% 
        c("flowCyto", "Flow cytometry") ~ "Flow cytometry"
    )
  )
```


```{r}
doseres_plot(gh2ax, 'all data', assay = 'γH2Ax_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
doseres_contrast(gh2ax, 'Exposure times and S9 status', assay = 'γH2Ax_Assay', color_col = 'Time of exposure [h]', linetype_col = 'Scoring technique', solid_level = 'Flow Cytometry', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
```


##Variance decomposition

```{r}
gh2axmod = gh2ax
names(gh2axmod) = make.names(names(gh2axmod))
```


```{r}
gh2aximp = mice(gh2axmod, m = 1, method = 'pmm', seed = 20260205)
gh2aximp = complete(gh2aximp, 1)

gh2aximp2 = prepare_varcomp(gh2aximp, gh2axmod)

gh2aximp2 = gh2aximp2[,c("Study.index", "Author", "DOI", "FC", "FClog", "Concentration.MMS", "Time.of.exposure..h.", "S9", "Relative.survival....", "Scoring.technique")]
any(is.na(gh2aximp2))
```


```{r,message=F,warning=F}
model_gh2ax = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2) +
       Time.of.exposure..h. +
       S9 + 
       Relative.survival.... +
       Scoring.technique +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = gh2aximp2
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_gh2ax))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

gh2axVAR = partR2(model_gh2ax, partvars = c(
                  "poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2)",
                  "Time.of.exposure..h.",
                  "S9",
                  "Relative.survival....",
                  "Scoring.technique"
                ))

gh2axVAR$R2
gh2axVAR$model = model_gh2ax
gh2axVAR$vc = vc
```




--------------
Mutation assay
--------------


##General data wrangling##

General first steps in data wrangling
```{r}
#Read in the data
muta = as.data.frame(read_excel(
  '../rawData/202604141723_Data_from_literature_search_MMS_TK6.xlsx',
  sheet = 'Forward gene mutation assay'))

#Perform general wrangling 
muta = generalwrangle(muta, conc_col = 'Concentration MMS', ctthresh = 10)

#Convert data classess
muta = correctclass(muta)
```


##Quality checks##

Check if the data classes are as desired
```{r}
str(muta)
```
Looks good


Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
muta[which(muta$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0),]
```
We see no subtraction from background


Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(muta$`Concentration MMS` == 0)
length(unique(muta$`Study index`))
```
Looks good


Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(muta$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```
We have no missing replicates


Let's remove any studies with too few observations now
```{r}
muta = remove_few_obs_studies(muta)
```



##Check outcome units##
```{r}
table(muta$`Outcome unit (eg Mutation frequency in percentage)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

The outcomes can generally be divided into two classes, one for the standard comet assay and one for the CBmuta assay, let's standardize the naming and convert promille measurements to percent measurements.
```{r}
muta = convert_muta_to_perm(muta)
```


##Conversions

Examine the different variability units that were used
```{r}
table(muta$`Outcome variability unit (eg std deviation)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```


Convert variability estimates to SDs and SEMs
```{r}
muta = convert_varest(muta)
```

Convert all responses to FC
```{r}
muta = convert_to_FC(muta, conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
```

Convert all concentrations to uM
```{r}
muta = convert_concs(muta, MMS_g_per_mol)
```

Standardize naming for cytotox assays
```{r}
muta = convert_CTassaytype(muta)
```

Standardize locus naming
```{r}
muta = convert_locus_naming(muta)
```


##Check for cytotoxicity

```{r}
table(muta$`Relative survival (%)`, useNA = 'ifany')
```

See where there is cytotoxicity data missing
```{r}
muta[,c(2:4)][is.na(muta$`Relative survival (%)`),]
```


The only missing datapoint for relative survival is from the Honma study, here, one concentration lower already causes a cytotox of nearly 20% so we may assume that this concentration is overly cytotoxic

```{r}
muta$ct = muta$`Relative survival (%)` >= 20 & !(is.na(muta$`Relative survival (%)`))
```

Percentage of data that remains after removing highly cytotoxic observations
```{r}
sum(muta$ct) / nrow(muta)
muta = muta[muta$ct == T,]
```

```{r}
muta = remove_few_obs_studies(muta)
```
 

#Plotting the data

Let's check for Authors that reported multiple experiments
```{r}
length(unique(muta$Author))
length(unique(muta$`Study index`))
```

```{r}
doseres_plot(muta, 'all data', assay = 'mutation_Assay', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
doseres_contrast(muta, 'Exposure time and expression period', assay = 'mutation_Assay', color_col = "Time of exposure [h]", shape_col = 'Expression period[days]', conc_col = 'Concentration MMS')
```

This all looks nice and comparable

#Variance decomposition

```{r}
mutamod = muta
names(mutamod) = make.names(names(mutamod)) 

mutamod = prepare_varcomp(mutamod)

mutamod = mutamod[,c("Study.index", "Author", "DOI", "Gene.locus", "Time.of.exposure..h.", "Expression.period.days.", "Concentration.MMS", "Relative.survival....", "Outcome.for.the.treatment", "replicates", "FC", "FClog")]

any(is.na(mutamod))
```

No imputation is needed because we have no missing data for any of the columns of interest

```{r,message=F,warning=F}
model_muta = lmer(
  FClog ~ poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2) +
       Time.of.exposure..h. +
       Expression.period.days. +
       Relative.survival.... +
       (1|Author/DOI/Study.index),
  data = mutamod
)

vc = as.data.frame(VarCorr(model_muta))
vcovtot = sum(vc$vcov)
vc$prop = vc$vcov / vcovtot

mutaVAR = partR2(model_muta, partvars = c("poly(Concentration.MMS, degree = 2)",
                               "Time.of.exposure..h.",
                               "Expression.period.days.",
                               "Relative.survival...."
                               ), R2_type = 'marginal')

mutaVAR$R2
mutaVAR$model = model_muta
mutaVAR$vc = vc
```

```{r}
#Read in the data
```

```{r}
str(CAA)
```
Looks good


Check whether (and if so, where) subtraction from background occurred
```{r}
CAA[which(CAA$`Outcome for the treatment` == 0),]
```

There is one observation with a 0 outcome however this is not due to subtraction from the background

Check if every observation has its own unique control
```{r}
sum(CAA$`Concentration MMS` == 0)
length(unique(CAA$`Study index`))
```
Looks good


Check for missing replicates
```{r}
table(CAA$replicates, useNA = 'ifany')
```

We have no missing replicates
